search_streams.coverage_note: Thirty-four canonical candidates have source-specific stimulus, neural-response, behavior and pain-boundary extraction. S776 distinguishes heat behavior from vibration calcium imaging; S777 has expression/GRASP evidence without a measured stimulus-evoked neural response; S778 gives peripheral nerve firing and rolling. S797 separates MD IV thermogenetic activation, chordotonal vibration, GCaMP signals, larval escape, EM anatomy and a simple steady-state rate model. Backward and forward citation screening remains open; no subjective-pain or human SCS inference follows. Two candidates, S794-S795, were independently reconciled from saved primary leads; both have relevant larval nociception behavior, neither has direct stimulus-evoked neural response. S797 was independently reconciled from the S282 v1 bibliography. S212/S282 citation relationship for S794-S795 remains unverified; count 27 is not an itemized inventory. Five independently checked bibliography leads and their scope/status are itemized in drosophila-nociception-audit.json, but they are only a partial screen and do not reconcile the aggregate 27. S282 v1 pp. 38 and 32 were checked against Pulver (2009; PMCID PMC2694103) and Ainsley et al. (2003; PMID 12956960). Pulver abstract and indexed figure legends indicate a neuronal activation/tool comparator without a direct noxious-stimulus assay; methods-level screen remains pending because the linked PMC author manuscript returned reCAPTCHA. Ainsley full publisher VoR PDF was checked via a Wayback capture: it reports spontaneous crawling, no direct neural recording, and a hot-probe comparison marked data not shown; S282 v1 p. 24 cites it as ppk-driver provenance in Methods/Fly Stocks, not as nociception evidence. S801 is a separate 2013 natural-wasp-attack study (PLOS DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0078704), published from S777 reference #9 after primary full-text review; class-IV perturbation and larval rolling are behavior evidence without direct neural recording. S802 (Pan et al. 2023, DOI 10.1016/j.cub.2023.02.032) was published from S769 References #46 after primary full-text review; it separates heat, gentle touch, C4da activation, A08n spikelets, Cho calcium signals, rolling and crawling. NS-03 now has 26 canonical candidates with four-field extraction. The independent 28-work bibliography has 11 exact DOI matches and 17 DOI-unmatched screened leads; one additional lead, Honjo and Tracey (2018; 10.1371/journal.pgen.1007464), has been selected for canonical-card review after independent full-text triage; it remains DOI-unmatched and is not yet a canonical source. The historical aggregate 27 remains unreconciled. S809 adds a checked author-manuscript card for Balboa/PPK mechanical nocifensive behavior; protein interaction is not evoked neural activity. NS-03 now has 28 canonical cards in the living audit, separate from its independent 28-work bibliography and unreconstructed historical 27-lead aggregate. S810 adds a checked Piezo larval mechanonociception card and separates ex-vivo ppk-neuron currents from in-vivo behavior; NS-03 now has 29 canonical cards. S811 adds a calibrated warm-water escape assay at about 29 C and separates water exposure from 70 C hotplate setting; no tissue-injury or subjective-pain measure is claimed. NS-03 now has 30 canonical cards. S812 adds the full-text RNAi thermal-nociception screen with separate 42/46 C protocols and explicit line-versus-animal denominators; NS-03 now has 31 canonical cards. S813 adds a source-card correction: 50 mN force directly evokes Class IV GCaMP3 optical activity in filleted larvae, separate from 30 mN rolling and 42 C thermal behavior; group Ns remain unavailable from Supplemental Table S2. NS-03 now has 32 canonical cards. S814 adds full-author-PDF Imambocus light-versus-50 mN touch circuit assays with separate optical neural activity, EM anatomy and behavior; NS-03 now has 33 canonical cards. The independent 28-work bibliography has 17 exact-DOI matches and 11 DOI-unmatched screened leads. The unreconstructed historical aggregate 27 and SRC-03 dependency remain open. S815 adds primary Zhong et al. thermal/mechanical larval behavior and separate S2R+ cell physiology; no in-vivo stimulus-evoked nociceptor recording or subjective-pain inference. The independent 28-work bibliography now has 18 exact-DOI matches and 10 DOI-unmatched screened leads; historical 27 remains separate. On 2026-09-27 S092 full text was rechecked and two newly carded primary experiments S822 and S823 added: local infrared heat or UVC input, distinct Class IV/mdIV extracellular neural recordings and larval protective behavior. Optical calcium, firing and behavior have assay-specific cohorts; none measures subjective pain. A separate Yoshino 2025 bioRxiv heat-off epidermal lead remains uncarded for later review. The historical 27-lead aggregate, incomplete primary snowballing and S740 lineage remain open. Two primary full-text forward-citation leads from S797 are now indexed as S827 and S828; this is bounded lead expansion, not a saturation claim. The complete S282 v1 JATS identity screen has 95 references; c62 and c66 were subsequently full-text screened and indexed as S833 and S834. S833 separates heat-probe rolling from dendrite morphology; S834 records only an assay-specific negative hot-probe behavior comparison. Both lack stimulus-evoked neural activity recordings. The historical 27-lead roster is unrecoverable and later-dated citation saturation remains open. S835 adds a distinct bioRxiv v1 heat-off preprint: epidermal GCaMP6s and separate rolling are indexed with exact figure locators; Figure 1 caption and Methods disagree on 30 s versus 10 s recovery. It is not direct neural recording, a version of S092, or evidence of human pain/ECAP/SCS. S839 adds Turner et al. 2016 from S835 JATS ref R6, with separate cold stimulus, class III calcium response and larval contraction locators; this is not subjective pain or human ECAP/SCS evidence. search_streams.coverage_note: S772 establishes cross-species structural comparison of mesoscale community motifs in published inter-areal connectomes. Its human functional-connectivity analysis is within human data; no Drosophila-to-human dynamical representation, causal-invariant, ECAP or SCS transfer is tested. Exact/synonym/author search and backward/forward citation screening remain open. S796 is a verified canine/human seizure-EEG transfer analogue with distinct unsupervised and semi-supervised target-trial scenarios; it does not validate fly-to-ECAP/SCS transfer. A 2026-09-27 primary review of the HIPPIE Nature article DOI 10.1038/s41467-026-76939-w, Results/Fig. 5 and Discussion, confirms trained macaque-to-mouse extracellular-neuron representation transfer but no labelled human neuronal training data, fly connectome, ECAP, pain or causal invariant. The TN-VAE bioRxiv v1 DOI 10.64898/2025.12.03.692227, Results 3.3/Fig. 3, pretrained on rat data and fine-tuned on 18 minutes of one human subject before testing two unseen humans; its abstract's zero-shot wording does not mean rat-to-human transfer without human fine-tuning. S821 is a corrected PLOS porcine-vagus eCAP physical observation model, not a learned cross-species representation, Drosophila connectome or human spinal SCS validation. These are bounded analogues; graph-motif and citation coverage and saturation remain open.

search_streams.coverage_note: EVOKE 3/12-month Lancet (S779), 24-month JAMA (S780) and 36-month RAPM (S781) reports are indexed as one randomized cohort, NCT02924129. The PA-04 pass also identified the Costandi sleep subanalysis (PMID 36437161; same cohort, PSQI; baseline ECAP-CL n=62 and 12-month n=55) and the Mekhail 24-month holistic IPD analysis (PMID 37491149; same cohort, not an independent trial). The seven-patient Falowski intraoperative neuromonitoring series (PMID 35088735) links to a larger-study registration, but patient-level overlap with the randomized efficacy sample is unestablished. The separate JAMA Figure 4C correction is S805, not a fourth trial report. The separate Springer method-label correction to S162 is S806 and supplies no replacement outcomes. The Lancet method is abstract-only here; JAMA full text distinguishes 134 randomized primary-outcome records from 92 24-month completers. The 36-month analysis was not prespecified and used LOCF. ECAP is feedback for the intervention, not a pain measure or baseline outcome predictor. Broader snowballing remains open.
